messages.author: 404.zero
messages.reply_to: @DisintegrationLoops | Hi! I’m also using a free version of cursor, and getting very bad results, it can’t make a simple particle cloud, is this a problem with how I’m prompting it
messages.text:
The free Cursor tier is really the main problem here. And if you were using Auto mode, then most likely you were not even using Claude at all — and definitely not Opus.

TouchDesigner tasks like this need much higher limits, and right now Claude is basically the only model that handles them reasonably well. Even then, it still needs a lot of guidance, simply because the model is not yet deeply trained on TD.

So the bad results are not just about your prompting — the free Cursor setup is a big limitation.

In practice, the paid version of Claude Code already gives much better limits and a much more acceptable quality of results.

Over time this should improve further as Anthropic uses more TouchDesigner documentation and the model becomes better grounded in it.

messages.author: twozero
messages.text:
hey everyone, quick note from the team. the tool is in active development, we're training, improving, and adding examples every day, and your feedback helps a ton. knowing what to focus on next vs what can wait is exactly why this community matters to us.
where we are right now: noding from scratch (placing specific nodes with exact parameters) is still the toughest challenge for any LLM, and we're working hard on it. but where twozero already works really well is editing existing projects, updating old patches, finding bugs, writing scripts and tools, integrations, porting between projects, understanding how your patch works, and learning TD in general without leaving the app.
so if you want to get the most out of it right now, feed it your existing projects and start asking questions. that's where the magic is )

messages.author: abhi
messages.text:
Hello, thank you so much for this tool. I have been battling with a problem since so long and it solved it in minutes. I would have never thought this is the problem specially being kinda new to TD

here is a summary of what happened (from claude): 
Problem: The blob tracking overlay disappeared when switching scenes through the SceneChanger, showing only the base video.

Cause: The operator doing the blob detection (script1) had no output wire connected to anything, so TouchDesigner never ran it unless the network was open in the editor.
Fix: Connected script1's output through a zero-opacity levelTOP into the final composite, giving TouchDesigner a reason to run it every frame — even when accessed through the SceneChanger.


This is amazing, thank you so much again!!

messages.author: verygeeky
messages.reply_to: @DRIFTKOP | Any best practices on how to use Claude? Have Opus make a plan, execute plan on lower models?
messages.text:
I've been burning a ton of tokens through this MCP server.  Others have said they've had better luck with modifications to existing projects or using it to build your understanding of and existing tox.  Again, I had pretty good luck with 'one-shot' or 3-4 iteration to get a vsiualization. 

My advice - get clarity on what you are attempting to build and focus on documenting that first.  As your project gets more complex, you want to have a clear set of expectations/tests that the model can use to validate or guide it's work.  I use "plan for scale, use containers, dats should be scoped apprpriately, if you can do something in 3 lines of python instead of a 10 node network, do so.  use screenshots and test logic to verify your networks..." and a handful of "advice from a seasoned td nerd" things i've heard to help it build a PRACTICES.md that the CLAUDE.md for a specific project can refer to.  Use git for supporting documentation.  Use plan mode.  Use SuperClaude or another framework for memory and context management.  Save often.  Remind yourself to play in TD 'by hand' too - imho the LLM is a terrible place for insipriation, but helps with some of the tedious refactoring / mapping tasks.

There's a bunch of hay that's been made of the claude-opus-4-6 to claude-opus-4-7 real-world performance fall off.  That experience has been mirrored in the MCP use, too.  It just got dumb.

messages.author: verygeeky
messages.text: have  it maintain and keep updated a TODO.md, BUGS.md,  or github issues so you can /reset your session context as often as you want without losing 'where you were'

messages.author: twozero-ai
messages.reply_to: @tiwonku |  [PLF],  | Etiqueta de servidor: PLF | PLF | it seems like most of the anti-ai discourse revolves around topics like artistic agency, purity, elbow grease, etc  i agree
messages.text:
The surveillance-state framing is harder to brush off than the "artistic purity" one.

Cloud-first today because that's where capability is. We want to build with the strongest models available, and those happen to be closed. We don't have the bandwidth to fine-tune or maintain our own open-source stack on top of everything else we're shipping.

The MCP architecture is model-agnostic. Nothing structural prevents plugging a local backend in once open-source models reliably handle tool-use at the level TD networks need.

We're artists first. We pick tools that speed up creative work, not tools defined by whether the underlying stack is open or closed. Our limited time with local models has gone more into setup and tinkering than into actual making. Cloud models let us get to the work sooner, so that's where we are.

There's also a hardware question. A 5090 is out of reach for most people. A100 or H100 setups, even more so. So "go local" today shifts the access problem somewhere else, not away.

If the community keeps growing and the local model space catches up, local backends will be on our radar. For now it's monitor, not invest.

you don't know and never will. only with fully open source software can you be 100% certain that there is no virus or other malware.

I think TWOZERO is a trustworthy brand (they have good intentions and have been in the community a long time), but even trustworthy brands can make mistakes. it is hard to ship 100% stable software by yourself. I make a similar tool and it is incredibly difficult to ensure full stability on aggressive development timelines for so many platforms/configurations. I have shipped many broken versions already, but my users are incredibly helpful and report the issues -- this helps a lot. and that is the most important thing anyone can do here: report the issues, while being as clear and helpful and neutral as possible.

it is important to be patient and kind to the developers. they are trying very hard to make something beautiful and useful. it is much harder than it looks

messages.author: rosco
messages.reply_to: @Danii |  [WIZ],  | Etiqueta de servidor: WIZ | WIZ | Dumber as in it's constantly going on wild goose chases looking at the wrong things and misconceptualizing the problems in net
messages.text:
probably a skills issue more than anything. well-defined skills and rules are quintessential to comprehension. context is king.

my go-to analogy here is: using AI is like hiring a contractor. the models are their education/background -- some went to amazing schools (fable), others went to so-so technical universities (sonnet).

now obviously you wanna hire somebody who is fluent in touch (Embody, TWOZERO, etc.), but every "contractor" is different, each has their own styles and approaches that you may or may not like. it's highly subjective. but there are certain objective truths and best-practices to follow in touch. so really, I think any model with sonnet 4.6+ capability, should execute decently in touch, with a well-defined skillset. but no skills/rules, and you are playing the lottery for whether it will hallucinate or research things or not. not all universities teach touch... and if they do, it's not usually to the extent that you need professioanlly, to truly "grok" it. that's where skills/rules come into play.
